userStories.title: Fix ralph.sh to block until Ralph process completes (sequential execution)
userStories.description:
File: ralph/ralph.sh

Problem: ralph.sh launches ralph.py with `nohup ... &` and then exits immediately (fire-and-forget). When a caller runs ralph.sh in a loop for multiple projects, all projects start simultaneously, creating multiple parallel requests to llama-server. llama-server is single-threaded and cannot handle parallel inference — this causes memory pressure, deadlocks, and failed stories.

Fix: Add a `wait $RALPH_PID` call after the nohup launch. This makes ralph.sh block until ralph.py exits, so sequential callers work correctly. The nohup is still needed (detaches from terminal session), but wait brings the shell back into sync with the process.

Current code (around line 69):
```bash
nohup $PYTHON "$RALPH_PY" "$SLUG" $EXTRA_ARGS >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &
RALPH_PID=$!
echo "Ralph started: PID=$RALPH_PID log=$LOG_FILE"
```

Replace with:
```bash
nohup $PYTHON "$RALPH_PY" "$SLUG" $EXTRA_ARGS >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &
RALPH_PID=$!
echo "Ralph started: PID=$RALPH_PID log=$LOG_FILE"

# Wait for Ralph to finish so sequential callers don't stack parallel runs
wait $RALPH_PID
RALPH_EXIT=$?
echo "Ralph finished: PID=$RALPH_PID exit=$RALPH_EXIT"
```

The log rotation block after should stay in place. Do NOT remove the `&` from nohup — that is still needed for nohup to work correctly. The `wait` is what makes the script synchronous.

Constraint: Only modify ralph/ralph.sh. Do not touch ralph.py or any other file.
